findings.where: evidence/logs/scroll_webkit.json, per_frame indices 5, 30, 54, 77, 102 ... 631 — every twenty-fifth frame of the 642 recorded during this scroll capture
findings.what: The framework's own build cost spikes to 916-1462 ms (median 1197 ms) on 26 of 642 frames, at a period of exactly 25 frames (gaps: 25,24,23,25,26,23,27,26,26,24,26,25,27,25,25,23,24,25,25,25,25,25,26,26,25), against a median build of 4 ms; those 26 frames hold 31,674 ms of the 36,583 ms of total build time, 87 per cent of it.
findings.why: Twenty-five driven steps is 400 ms of app time, so the year-deep thread stops for over a second to rebuild roughly every 0.4 s of scrolling; the clip cannot show it because the clock is driven and the harness waits for every frame, so the perfect motion I measured proves position fidelity and not frame budget, and the log's no-GPU caveat covers raster (median 176 ms) but not a Dart-side build that is 300x its own median on a fixed period.

findings.where: the query sheet at y=326-497 and the fifteen filter strips running from y=570 to y=2421 of 3120
findings.what: Search chrome fills 67.1 per cent of the screen (2095 of 3120 px). The first result starts at y=2518, 80.7 per cent of the way down, so of the ten hits logs/12_search.report.json records for the query 'rain', one is readable and the second is cut in half by the tab bar at y=2976. No chip carries a selected state — EVERYTHING, WRITTEN, PHOTOGRAPHS and the other twelve are drawn in the same stock, the same ink and the same weight — and the hit count appears nowhere on the glass. The PHOTOGRAPHS and VIDEO filters exist but no artifact shows a media search returning anything: 12's kinds are message 8, ritual_kept 1, todo_event 1.
findings.why: A searchable year is the reason to keep a year, and a search that shows one hit in ten, with no count, no visible filter state and no pictured media result, is a reason to go back to a search that works.

findings.where: the whole frame — thresholding at luma 150 finds exactly three elements: the print (y=371 down), the caption slip at y=2420-2779, and the 'put it back' line below it
findings.what: logs/14_media_viewer.report.json records this frame as kind 'video', initialised and playing, at position_ms 1530 of duration_ms 2500. Nothing on the glass says it is a video, where it is in it, or how to pause, scrub, replay or mute it. The only control is 'put it back'. There is no next or previous, and no counter, against the 183 media items logs/04_moments.report.json counts in the same store.
findings.why: The row names the media viewer as a capability that has to be dependable; a video that cannot be paused, scrubbed, identified as a video or stepped past is the viewer failing at the one thing a person opens it to do.

findings.where: "scroll_emulator": {"missing": "no Android device was up in this session"}, MANIFEST.json missing 16_setup_android.png, and the "browser" field of all eighteen scene logs
findings.what: Every one of the fifteen captured artifacts is the web build under headless WebKit at 360x780 or 480x1040, dpr 3; the only non-WebKit record in evidence/logs is reception.json, on Chromium. No artifact and no measurement shows the messenger running on Android, and the one scroll measurement that would have says no device was up.
findings.why: Half the mission is an Android app, so for one of the two people every capability and every performance claim in this row is untested and unphotographed.

findings.where: MANIFEST.json "stale": written 2026-09-07T22:24:14Z against a capture that began 2026-09-08T06:05:04Z — with 12_search.png (22:22:09Z), 14_media_viewer.png (22:24:51Z), 10_first_run.png (22:25:04Z) and 06_unfolding.mp4 (2026-09-08T00:11:52Z)
findings.what: The five artifacts that carry the messenger's delivery states, its search, its media viewer, its empty state and its arriving message all predate this capture by 5h53m to 7h43m, while 02_chat.png — the one chat still that was re-shot in this run — came back changed against the baseline at SSIM 0.648 (DIFF.json), far under the 0.999 the diff calls 'nothing a person would see has moved'. findings.where: "transport": "local", host address 127.0.0.1:41497, and the embedded "tailscale" block
findings.what: The whole capability matrix — send, ack, read, reply, react, edit, delete, typing, voice_note, video, viewer, search, draft_survival, kill_mid_send, offline_queue (26 events), reconnect_ordering (seq 1..173 gapless) and host_offline_outbox — was produced by app/test/reliability_test.dart, a headless spine and transport test over loopback, not through the interface. findings.where: MANIFEST.json "missing": "not captured this session"; DIFF.json label "absent", "not captured in this session or the last"
findings.what: The artifact meant to show both devices has been absent for at least two cycles and the reason given names no cause — it states that it was not done, not why. No other artifact shows one message on two screens, so the read marker is only ever seen from the sending side.
findings.why: A read marker is trustworthy only if the other end can be seen agreeing with it, and nothing in the evidence shows the other end.

findings.where: the four state rows between y=1180 and y=2350, read against logs/13_messenger_states.report.json
findings.what: The glass draws 'read ✓✓' twice, 'it would not go ✗' in red on 'sending you the roster', and 'going ⦀' on 'ok — leaving now'. The report's states_on_the_glass is {read: 3, sent: 1, refused: 1}: it records a row as 'sent' when no 'sent ✓' appears anywhere in the frame, and it never records 'sending', which is the state whose word is 'going'. Separately, 'waiting to send' — the queued state a message sits in while the other phone is out of reach — is in the string table but appears in no artifact in the evidence.
findings.why: The artifact named for the messenger's states and its own record of those states disagree about which state a row is in, and the one state that matters when the link is down has never been photographed.

findings.where: the "end" field across the 300 entries of logs/11_chat_scroll.fling.json
findings.what: The thread's own estimate of where its end lies swings between 303,766 and 631,730 logical px, a factor of 2.08; it is revised on 94 of the 299 transitions, with single-frame revisions up to 59,324 px, while the thread itself travelled 8,439 px in total, 1.9 per cent of the mean estimate. There is no scroll position indicator on the glass: the rightmost 24 px of the thread band are unchanged across all 300 frames, mean luma 90.7 at frames 0, 50, 150 and 299.
findings.why: In a thread 8,069 rows deep nothing tells a person where they are, and the app cannot say how far there is to go to within a factor of two while they scroll it.

findings.where: the arrived notes at frames 162 and 326, the settled frames of the two unfolds
findings.what: A note that arrives through the fold settles as a mathematically straight rectangle: over 282 and 415 sampled rows its left edge has a standard deviation of 0.06 and 0.00 px and its right edge 0.49 and 0.50 px, while 'sending you the roster' in the same frame varies by 63 px on the left and 75 px on the right (sd 13.3 and 28.2). The second one, 'and the bread · Thu 3 Sep · 20:00', leaves roughly three quarters of its sheet blank below a single line of text.
findings.why: The newest message in the thread never comes to look like any other message in it, and a sheet three quarters empty under one line reads as a message that has not finished arriving.

findings.where: the last row of tiles, y≈2700-2935, fully above the tab bar at y=2964
findings.what: Two fully visible tiles carry no image and no placeholder text: mean luma 220.5 and 223.4 with sd 26.2 and 30.3, against 135.0 with sd 70.3 for the photo tile beside them. logs/04_moments.report.json records tiles_built 26 with blobs asked 18, arrived 18, reading 0, waiting 0 — eight built tiles with nothing in them and nothing saying so, though S.fetching ('still fetching the picture.') exists in the string table.
findings.why: Nothing on the glass distinguishes a tile that is still coming from one that is broken, which is the same failure as a spinner that outstays its welcome, taken from the other side.

findings.where: logs/02_chat.json "load": {"ms": 13712, "store": "fresh"}, with logs/01_pulse.json at 13209 ms and the eleven kept-store scenes between 2754 and 3356 ms
findings.what: First launch against the seeded year takes 13.2-13.7 s to become usable, and a warm launch 2.75-3.36 s. No artifact shows what is on the glass during either.
findings.why: 'No spinner that outstays its welcome' cannot be checked against any picture, and thirteen seconds is a long time to be looking at whatever is there.

what_is_working: The scroll itself is genuinely, measurably clean. I cross-correlated the 300 frames of 11_chat_scroll.mp4 against the app's own fling log and the painted content moved by exactly the amount the log claims on all 299 transitions: mean error -0.004 device px, p95 0.18 px, worst 0.33 px, over shifts from 31 to 143 px. Nothing pops in either — the largest frame-to-frame change in paper coverage is 0.052 of the band per 100 px moved, p50 0.013 — so notes are drawn complete as they enter.

Eleven of the twelve capabilities the row names are visible somewhere: text and photos (11_chat_scroll frame 100, 'Sun 26 Apr · 07:04 read ✓✓' under a photo), video (14 and the play mark in 04), voice notes (02_chat, a waveform and 0:26), reactions (02_chat, an object on the sheet at 15:14), replies (13's composer, 'answering leaving now. dont cut the end …'), delivery and read state, typing ('noor writing…' in 06 and 07), editing ('edited ↵' in 13), deleting ('took this back' in 13), full-text search (12, hits highlighted in the result), and the media viewer.

The five delivery states are separated by mark as well as by word — one tick for sent, two in ballpoint for read, a red cross for refused, a run of ticks for going — so a message that failed does not look like one that was read. A taken-back row correctly drops its delivery mark and keeps its time.

Sender is legible without relying on alignment: the two hands are distinct, and the delivery footer only appears under one of them. Measured, the positional difference is small — mine sit 33 logical px further from the left edge than theirs in 02_chat — so the hand is carrying it, and it does.

Ordering is monotonic everywhere it can be read: 02_chat 15:14 → 19:36, 13 17:19 → 19:40, 06 19:40 → 19:48 → 20:00, and 11_chat_scroll 22 Apr → 27 Apr across its seven throws. No timestamp changes between frames and no message appears twice.
Every note carries its own date and time, so a year-deep thread stays locatable in time even without a sticky day header.
The empty chat in 10_first_run says "first one's yours." with no product voice and no false state.

frames.json's held-frame test is honest and my eye agrees with it: every clip reports zero repeated frames, and I measured 10 per cent of pixels still changing by more than two grey levels on the last frames of 06, so nothing is being held.
verdict: The inventory is close to complete and the one thing this row is usually worst at is the thing this build is best at: I measured the dense scroll frame by frame against the app's own fling log and the picture moves exactly as far as the app says it does, to a third of a device pixel, with no pop-in and no held frames. But the row is decided by whether anything here sends a person back to Instagram, and three things do. Search finds ten and shows one, with two thirds of the screen given to fifteen filter strips that do not say which of them is on. The media viewer is playing a video, at 1.53 s of 2.50 s by its own report, with no play, no pause, no scrubber, no duration, no next, and nothing at all on the glass saying it is a video. And the framework's own timing log shows the thread stopping to build for 916 to 1462 ms on exactly every twenty-fifth frame — 400 ms of app time apart, 87 per cent of all build time in 4 per cent of the frames — which the clip cannot contradict, because the clip's clock is driven and the harness waits for every frame it takes. Underneath that is an evidence problem I cannot look past: the four stills that carry the states, the search, the viewer and the empty chat all predate this capture by most of a day, while the one chat still that was re-shot came back at SSIM 0.648, so those are pictures of a chat that has since changed; the offline-and-reconnect claim exists only as a headless unit test over 127.0.0.1; the tailnet run in evidence is three days old and moved four events, none of them media; and there is still no picture of two devices and nothing at all showing the messenger on Android. What is on the glass is good work. What the row asks — that every capability is dependable, on both phones, when the link drops — is not shown, and what is shown includes three failures that would each be reason enough to open the other app.
